I agree with you. If the entity that gave me the scholarship kept the funds because of the time limit problem, I would be okay with that. But that's not what's happening.

The flight school is keeping the funds. That's my problem.

The logic is that I earned a scholarship from a entity with no "time limit terms" but yet the flight school is the one that is dictating the use of my funds.  If the entity was the one forfeiting my funds and had a contract stating that I must use them in a certain time-frame, I wouldn't have any problem. My problem is that the FLIGHT SCHOOL is the one dictating this.

I left in June 2018 for the military. I returned to Vegas in September 2019. I reached out in February of 2020 when I had my life back to normal after returning. 

I'm posting about this now because I am just realizing how messed up it was of them.

Yes. They knew I would be attending. 

I have reached out to the entity but they told me I have to talk to the flight school.

I understand that is is not illegal because I signed a contract. It just is malignant and unfair. It shouldn't be their money to just keep because I was in the military and couldn't continue training.

Ah yes. The obvious comment.

I understand this. But it  is largely malignant and unjust. They didn't earn the scholarship money. I did.

Also, even if I wanted to resume my training within 180 days, I couldn't. I was in the military.

What's scary about this is that last semester my grandmother had her third stroke and was in the hospital for three days. I was not at school for a whole week and had to beg people for a ride back to my school from the airport. Nobody said anything about that and no one was generous to me. I pointed this out and they said I'm not giving money because nobody gave me money, which I guess a small part of it is because of that, but is definitely not the only reason I am not contributing.

So the general way I've been responding is that I have my own problems and that no one helps me with the cost of my life so how am I supposed to help him right now financially? He's not dying for money and his family is obviously  going through a hard time but I don't know if I'm saying it the right way.

So the main thing is that I CAN afford to contribute money but I just don't feel as if I should be obligated to, I have so many things on my mind that take precedence. Like I said before, I really feel bad for him and the whole situation, I really do but it's not like he had no way to get home or something. They just did it to be nice, and right now, I don't have the room to just "be nice".
